newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian MPS query Di Rupo child sex abuse charges.
newsitem.headline: Belgian MPS query Di Rupo child sex abuse charges.

text.p: Two members of a special Belgian parliamentary commission examining anonymous allegations that Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo had sex with under-age boys questioned the quality of the case against him on Tuesday.

Whatever the parliamentary commission decides on Di Rupo -- to reject the allegations, to uphold them and indict him or to ask for more investigations -- must then be put to a full parliamentary vote.

"The second file is very different from the first case. It consists of various items of dubious value," Francophone Socialist member of parliament Serge Moureaux told Reuters just before fellow Francophone Socialist Di Rupo began to give evidence to the commission.
The Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, said on Monday the allegations in the first file against Di Rupo, based on statements from a sole witness, were baseless.
However, it asked the commission to study the second file.
"The second file is even lighter than the first," Flemish Socialist member of the commission Renaat Landruyt told Reuters.

He said the file consisted of transcripts of anonymous telephone calls and anonymous letters, the validity of which was even harder to check than the statements made by witness Oliver Trugsnach in the first case file.
Di Rupo, a homosexual, has always denied child sex abuse.

There have been floods of denunciations of all types and against all sorts of people as a tide of hysteria has swamped the country following the discovery in August of an unconnected murderous paedophile ring led by rapist Marc Dutroux.
Last month Marie-France Botte, a prominent child rights campaigner, appealed for calm in the face of what she said were hundreds of letters a day containing all sorts of denunciations.
A police hot line set up in August in the wake of the Dutroux revelations has received thousands of calls -- some of them about Di Rupo.

The Di Rupo affair has been another nail in the coffin of Belgian public confidence that has been shaken since the arrest of Dutroux, the subsequent rescue of two young girls and discovery of the bodies of four more.
